round1_to_round2.convergence_assessment: This is mostly anchoring on shared inputs, not independent agreement. The fair-value spread fell from $32 to $8, and the cross-agent dispersion of P(>=148) fell from 0.027 to 0.011. All five round-2 files use my round-1 clean Q3 base ($0.77), roughly $5 of net cash and an early-September $92 low for the thesis break. Their 1-month ladders are almost copies of mine: P(>=147.90) ranges 0.495-0.505 against my 0.500. Source overlap more than doubled (mean Jaccard 0.067 to 0.166). The six URLs newly cited by 3+ agents are exactly my round-1 sources (Stock Taper, Teleborsa, TrendForce, Investing.com DB note, both 10-Qs), and agents 1 and 2 cite my file or my Twelve Data check as a source. The anchor itself is now confirmed: the Q2 call transcript (AllMind) has the CFO saying the baseline is ~51% at Q2 volumes and that the Q3 guide includes $7-9M (~300bp) of IEEPA refunds. So the convergence is on a correct number, but it counts as one original, not five. Independent work in round 2 was real but narrow: agent_1 (start-up costs inside non-GAAP, primary), agent_3 (cash-flow statement, primary), agent_5 (own multiple history, company releases), agent_2 (HBM4 test intensity, Korean localization) and agent_4 (SBC). Every agent landed below my $135, mostly by adding a Technoprobe multiple haircut on top of a Technoprobe-trimmed revenue path, which partly double-counts. That shading is not evidence. I therefore give the tighter round-2 consensus no extra confidence.

disagreements.topic: Farmers Branch start-up costs: already in non-GAAP results? (agent_1)
disagreements.positions: Agent_1: the $4.9M (Q2) and $11.9M (H1) start-up costs are inside non-GAAP opex, so moving them into COGS lowers GM, not EPS. Agents 3 and 4 treat the move into COGS as an EPS headwind during the FY27 ramp.
disagreements.resolution: Agent_1 is right. The Q2 8-K reconciliation adds back only restructuring, SBC, amortization and deal costs, so non-GAAP opex of $65.654M includes the $4.859M of start-up costs. The 10-Q says these costs 'will move to cost of revenues as the production ramps begin' (late Q4 FY26). The CFO expects $25-30M of pre-production cost in 2026 ($12M through Q2, about $7M in Q3) and says the site becomes GM-accretive once it reaches initial target capacity at the beginning of 2028. Carlsbad stops manufacturing in December 2026. So the clean $0.77 base already carries roughly $0.07/quarter of after-tax start-up drag. NTM EPS at Oct 2027 (Q4 FY27-Q3 FY28) should get part of it back. That argues against the lowest EPS paths (agents 3 and 4 at $4.15) and supports ~$4.30.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 FY26 8-K Ex. 99.01 non-GAAP reconciliation; 10-Q Q2 FY26 (factory start-up costs, Farmers Branch); Q2 call transcript

disagreements.resolution: I keep ~$4.30. From the clean $0.77 at $270M, ~25% revenue growth to ~$337M/quarter at ~40% incremental non-GAAP operating margin adds ~$0.29/quarter, giving ~$1.06/quarter or ~$4.2/year. Adding back part of the ~$0.07/quarter start-up drag as Farmers Branch absorbs gives ~$4.3-4.4. The risks are DRAM flattening sequentially (+2.5% q/q in Q2) and memory capex digestion. The range of $4.15-4.35 is about ±2.5% of value, which is small next to the multiple and the cycle.

key_drivers: Clean earnings power: the CFO's ~51% baseline GM at Q2 volumes. The Q3 54% guide includes $7-9M (~300bp) of IEEPA refunds, and Q2's 53.3% also had refunds plus Baldwin Park metal reclaim. The clean run rate is ~$0.77/quarter.

Farmers Branch: $25-30M of pre-production cost in 2026 is already inside non-GAAP opex. It moves into COGS from late Q4 FY26 and becomes GM-accretive from the beginning of 2028, a partial EPS tailwind inside the Oct-2027 NTM window.
Mix: DRAM/HBM +49% y/y but flat q/q in Q2; Foundry & Logic +22% y/y and +10% q/q, while Technoprobe grows +42% in logic. HBM share is strong at two of three makers.
Multiple: ~48x clean run-rate EPS today. The last peak-earnings top (2021) was ~32x realized forward EPS, so 30x NTM at Oct 2027 implies a roughly flat-to-lower price even with ~40% EPS growth.
Cyclicality: two ~61% drawdowns in five years and -49% within 2026. The Nvidia second source rests on one sell-side note (DB, 9/30); Nvidia was 10.2% of revenue in Q1 2026 only.

fair_value.reason: Clean NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct 2027 of ~$4.30 (clean Q3 base $0.77; ~25% revenue growth; ~40% incremental margin; partial Farmers Branch absorption from early 2028) x 30x = $129, plus ~$5 of net cash per share ($334M at 6/27/26 + FCF, over ~80M diluted shares) = ~$134. I trim to $133 for SBC (~$0.35/share after tax a year treated as free in non-GAAP EPS) and for FCF cross-checks of $104-128 after correcting agent_3's SBC double count. This is below my round-1 $135 and above the round-2 mean of $131.6, which stacks Technoprobe haircuts on both growth and multiple.

summary: After round 2 the five forecasters agree tightly ($128-136 fair value; P(close >= $148 on 2027-10-02) about 0.46), but most of that agreement comes from adopting my round-1 clean-EPS base. That base is now confirmed by the CFO's remarks on the Q2 call (~51% baseline GM; the Q3 guide includes $7-9M of IEEPA refunds), so it is one checked fact, not five. New primary checks cut both ways. Farmers Branch start-up costs are already in non-GAAP results and turn accretive from early 2028, which slightly supports EPS. DRAM/HBM revenue was flat quarter on quarter in Q2 while logic grew more slowly than Technoprobe. My fair value is about $133 against $149.15, and I leave the ladder at the forecasters' mean. FORM has no checked edge over the S&P 500 at this price, and the Q3 print (likely Oct 28) is the next real test.
